# Fasting vs. calorie restriction for weight loss: Which one wins?
## News briefs
If you're tired of counting calories to lose weight, you might consider a style of intermittent fasting called 4:3. It allows you to eat normally on four days of the week, and eat very little (fast) on the other three days, which can be spread throughout the week.
This approach might even help you lose more weight than counting calories, notes a small randomized controlled trial published in the May 20, 2025, issue of _Annals of Internal Medicine_ .

# Intermittent fasting more effective for weight loss than calorie-counting
A recent study — published in the journal [Annals of Internal Medicine](https://www.acpjournals.org/doi/10.7326/ANNALS-24-01631) in April 202 [...truncated by sanitizer]

answer:
Yes. A small 2025 trial of 165 people found that 4:3 intermittent fasting led to about 6 more pounds of weight loss after one year than daily calorie restriction [1]. The 4:3 group had a -7.6% change in body weight at 12 months, versus -5% in the calorie restriction group [5]. 58% of the fasting group achieved at least 5% weight loss at 12 months, compared with 47% in the calorie restriction group [5].

A systematic review and meta-analysis concluded that intermittent fasting appears slightly advantageous over energy restriction for body weight and cardiometabolic factors [4]. Another meta-analysis found that intermittent fasting may be superior to continuous calorie restriction for weight loss in some respects [3]. However, a review of existing evidence concluded that, overall, intermittent fasting produced as much weight loss as calorie restriction [6]. That review noted that alternate-day fasting specifically seemed to lead to greater weight loss than calorie restriction [6].
